analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only. docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one row at head line 1751 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP in the daemon-environment passthrough table. docs/provider/direct-mode.md revises the standalone preload step so it describes a load-time shape warmup, and the 5-second sweep tick warming deferred engines once the server is idle.

No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator wire behavior changes in this PR. Relevant threat IDs reviewed: TB-007, T-029 and T-041. The docs claim the warmup may precede the local listener opening, and that a request arriving first preempts an idle-time warmup. The warmup is described as a shader-cache probe plus shape cells, with no prompt data or KV caches involved. The docs do not say whether it uses synthetic inputs only and never touches the SSD prefix cache, so I cannot confirm T-041 is unaffected. If it did donate synthetic prefixes to the cache, that would affect the TTFT oracle and at-rest cache surface. That would need checking in the implementation in ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, which is outside the supplied evidence.

The new env var DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP appears in the table of variables read by the CLI and daemon. The table does not state that it is forwarded to the LaunchAgent; the surrounding prose says `darkbloom start` copies only listed passthrough keys, so the row implies it is. That is a performance and availability switch, not a trust input.

The remaining integration question is whether the warmup runs under an attested serving state or touches cache or KV state. That is not verifiable from the supplied docs. No concrete security regression is identified.
